result.topic_en: Euler explains the third part of the variation, the term involving the second differential of y, interprets it geometrically as the deviation of the direction of the varied curve element from the original tangent, and notes that it vanishes when the tangents are parallel.
result.transcription:
62 METHODVS NOVA CALCVLVM
punctis proportionalis fuerit, functioni cuicunque binarum variabilium $x$ et $y$, tum
$V\,dx\sqrt{(1+pp)}$
exprimit elementum temporis ideoque formula
$\int V\,dx\sqrt{(1+pp)}$,
totum tempus quo corpus ab A ad M peruenit.

Explicatio partis tertiae in variatione.
44. Quod ad tertiam partem variationis attinet scilicet
$dt\left(\frac{ddy}{dx\,dt}\right)\left(Q-\frac{dR}{dx}+\frac{ddS}{dx^2}\text{ etc.}\right)$
ea locum non habet, nisi expressio Z etiam differentialia secundi gradus inuoluat, quod quidem rarissime vsu venire solet. Hic autem obseruandum est, quoniam $M\mu = dt\left(\frac{dy}{dt}\right)$ fore pro sequenti elemento
$m\omega = dt\left(\frac{dy}{dt}\right)+dt\,dx\left(\frac{ddy}{dx\,dt}\right)$
vnde colligitur
$dt\left(\frac{ddy}{dx\,dt}\right)=\frac{m\omega - M\mu}{dx}=\frac{M\omega - M\mu}{Pp}$,
hac autem formula exprimitur declinatio directionis $\mu\omega$ a directione $Mm$, quae quidem, vt iam ante obseruauimus semper est quam minima.

45. Quodsi ergo Tangens in $\mu$ perfecte fuerit parallela tangenti in M, quod euenit, si etiam in curua generatrice BN, tangens ad N huic fuerit parallela, tum variatio ex tertia parte oriunda prorsus euanescit, quod etiam de termino initiali A est intelligendum, si tangentes in A et B inter se
fuerint

items.quote: ea locum non habet, nisi expressio Z etiam differentialia secundi gradus inuoluat, quod quidem rarissime vsu venire solet.
items.english: It has no place unless the expression Z also involves differentials of the second order, which indeed very rarely happens in practice.

items.quote: hac autem formula exprimitur declinatio directionis $\mu\omega$ a directione $Mm$, quae quidem, vt iam ante obseruauimus semper est quam minima.
items.english: This formula expresses the deviation of the direction μω from the direction Mm, which, as we observed before, is always infinitely small.

items.quote: Quodsi ergo Tangens in $\mu$ perfecte fuerit parallela tangenti in M, quod euenit, si etiam in curua generatrice BN, tangens ad N huic fuerit parallela, tum variatio ex tertia parte oriunda prorsus euanescit
items.english: If therefore the tangent at μ is exactly parallel to the tangent at M, which happens if in the generating curve BN the tangent at N is also parallel to it, then the variation arising from the third part vanishes entirely.
